note:
Reviewed CDB90 match 327, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: Exact linked article, named engagement and complete source first/last day match the catalogue. The row is parentless, with no competing source row for this target. Preserve the two original source NAM force identities; counts remain CDB estimates.

Equipment review: the CDB90 TK ARMY OF PALESTINE retains its aggregate identity and all numerical estimates. The Ottoman infantry illustration uses a representative WWI Mauser-and-cloth-cap component. AWM identifies the Model 1893 as a standard WWI rifle, shows soldiers of the 125th Infantry Regiment in 1915, and preserves a soldier’s serge cap collected in Palestine in 1918. These establish an equipment family, not the exact clothing or weapon of every Gaza defender, the share of infantry, or a reconstruction of the complete Ottoman force. AWM photographs demonstrate varied caps, shirts and coats; machine guns, artillery, attached German troops and individual dress are not assigned this uniform. The AWM Gaza account identifies the Ottoman 1917 defensive force independently of the CDB personnel quantities.
